svg.title: rondOfeed wiring layout
svg.text: Top view, rear wall at the top. Both drawings have the same orientation. Hole positions and board outlines come from the Adafruit PCB files.
To scale. Plate, disc and lid removed.
Component side, 15 rows, 43.2 × 50.8 mm. Columns A–E and F–J are separate. Rails are not connected to each other.
• Proposal, not built or tested. Check it against your parts before soldering.
• Breakout: one 10-pin header in F3–F12. The terminal pins line up with holes A5–A10. Solder them if they reach, for support. Leave A5–E10 empty.
• Put a spacer under the terminal edge if those pins do not reach. The terminal screws press on an otherwise one-sided mount.
• Fit the jumpers, R1 and D1 first. Column G is half under the breakout.
• INDEX and UART stay unconnected. Bend the C1 leads to fit the rail spacing.
• Converter shown as a 3-pin in-line module, 11.5 × 7.5 mm (example: R-78E5.0-0.5). Check its pin order. It sits flipped: IN in row 15.
• The ground link runs along the front edge of the board, the 12 V feed round the rear corner, so both stay clear of the M3 screws.
• GP2 to GP6 are on the wall side of the Pico, so those wires go round its front end. Keep them away from the antenna at that end.
